### Miracle at Meribah
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/miracle-at-meribah-one-year-devotions-for-men-july-27.html
Passage: Numbers 20:10, 12
Points:
- Faced with an acute water shortage, Israel responded by complaining bitterly against Moses and Aaron.
- God directed Moses to speak directly to the rock before the congregation to provide water.
- Moses allowed frustration to govern his words, addressing the assembly as rebels and claiming credit for the miracle.
- By dishonoring the Lord's unique holiness before the people, Moses forfeited entry into the Promised Land.
- Hasty words and unchecked temper can cause leaders to miss out on God's highest blessings.

### Anger’s Bitter Fruit
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-apr-22-2008-11573880.html
Passage: Numbers 20:1-13
Points:
- Moses succumbed to unchecked anger and preached a hostile, unauthorized sermon to the people.
- Driven by rage, Moses struck the rock twice rather than simply speaking to it.
- Moses' rhetoric flirted with blasphemy by taking personal credit for bringing water from the rock.
- Despite Moses' sinful outburst and unbelief, God graciously caused streams of water to flow abundantly.
- The Lord often provides lavish grace to His people even amid human failure and spiritual carnality.

### Devotional: Numbers 20
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numb-20-psalms-58-59-isa-98-104-james-3/
Passage: Numbers 20:1-13
Points:
- The Israelites reacted to real physical thirst with bitter accusations rather than seeking God in faith.
- Worn down by decades of grumbling, Moses reacted with pretension and struck the rock twice.
- The root of Moses' sin was failing to trust God and uphold His holiness before Israel.
- Moses' failure to reach Canaan illustrates that the old covenant could never fully transform the human heart.
- Christ is the true Rock who was struck once for all to pour out living water.

### Great Losses, Severe Mercies, Tearful Joy
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/great-losses-severe-mercies-tearful-joy
Passage: Numbers 20:12
Points:
- Moses failed to honor God's transcendent holiness when he struck the rock instead of speaking to it.
- Denying Moses entrance into Canaan was an act of severe mercy rather than harsh cruelty.
- Because profaning God's holiness warranted death, Moses received a gracious reprieve instead of immediate execution.
- God's painful discipline in the lives of believers always carries a loving, protective purpose.
- Believers can experience tearful joy under heartbreaking losses by trusting God's sovereign mercy.
